question: How does instruction finetuning scale with the number of finetuning tasks, model size and the inclusion of chain-of-thought data, and does it generalize across model families?
hypothesis: Scaling tasks and model size, and adding CoT data to the mixture, improves held-out performance in zero-shot, few-shot and CoT settings.
contributions: Study scaling of instruction finetuning in model size (8B, 62B, 540B) and number of tasks (9 to 1,836)
Show finetuning on nine CoT datasets preserves and improves reasoning on held-out tasks, while non-CoT-only finetuning degrades CoT
Release Flan-T5 checkpoints (80M to 11B) and train Flan-PaLM, Flan-cont-PaLM, Flan-U-PaLM

method.summary: Instruction-finetune T5, PaLM, cont-PaLM and U-PaLM on a mixture of Muffin, T0-SF, NIV2 and CoT collections (1,836 tasks) with a constant learning rate and Adafactor, then evaluate on held-out MMLU, BBH, TyDiQA and MGSM, plus a 190-example human preference study and responsible-AI benchmarks.
method.task: multi-task instruction finetuning of pretrained LMs; held-out task generalization

datasets.name: Muffin
datasets.size: 80 tasks (69 datasets, 27 categories); 62 tasks from Wei et al. 2021 plus 26 new
datasets.source: Wei et al. 2021 plus dialog and program-synthesis data

datasets.name: NIV2 (Natural Instructions v2)
datasets.size: 1,554 tasks (372 datasets, 108 categories) after removing 44 MMLU-related tasks

datasets.name: CoT mixture
datasets.size: 9 datasets, 9 tasks, 74,730 examples (AQuA 2,715; CREAK 6,910; ECQA 7,110; ESNLI 36,170; GSM8K 7,470; QASC 1,080; QED 5,145; Sensemaking 6,070; StrategyQA 2,060)
datasets.preprocessing: about ten manually written instruction templates per dataset

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.split: 5-shot, few-shot exemplars from dev set; validation set reported except Tables 1 and 4 (test)

datasets.name: Open-ended set
datasets.size: 190 examples (5 categories of 20, 60 CoT variants, 30 few-shot)

other.T5 baseline: LM-adapted, 100B extra tokens of C4 with LM objective (Lester 2021)

training.objective: supervised next-token loss on instruction/target pairs (inferred: standard seq2seq or causal LM loss; inputs separated from targets by end-of-sequence token)
training.lr: T5: 5e-4; PaLM 8B and 62B and cont-PaLM: 3e-3; PaLM 540B and U-PaLM 540B: 1e-3 (Table 22)
training.batch_size: global batch 64 for Flan-T5, 32 for Flan-PaLM and variants (Table 22); packing makes effective size larger
training.steps: Flan-T5 Small 98k, Base 84k, Large 64k, XL 38k, XXL 14k; Flan-PaLM 8B 40k, 62B 40k, 540B 21k; Flan-cont-PaLM 62B 60k; Flan-U-PaLM 540B 30k
training.tokens: 1.4B tokens for PaLM finetuning (0.2% of 780B pretraining tokens)
training.dropout: 0.05 for all except 0.1 for Flan-PaLM 540B and Flan-U-PaLM 540B
training.regularisation: packing with attention masking across example boundaries
training.hardware: about 512 TPU v4 chips for 37 hours (Flan-PaLM 540B)
training.compute: Table 2: Flan-PaLM 540B 5.6E+21 FLOPs finetune vs 2.5E+24 pretrain (0.2%)

other.checkpoint selection: single checkpoint per model chosen from periodic evaluations (every 2k to 10k steps) on held-out tasks; same step count across ablations
other.mixture caps: Muffin 30,000, T0-SF 20,000, CoT 100,000, NIV2 5,000 examples per task (Table 23)
other.task order for scaling: CoT, Muffin, T0-SF, NIV2 added sequentially

inference.decoding: human eval: temperature sampling, 5 responses, pick best log-probability without length normalisation after filtering scores better than half of the median; benchmarks: not stated
inference.temperature: 0.7 (open-ended human eval); toxicity eval 1.0 with top-k 40
inference.samples: 5 samples per prompt in human eval; 25 continuations per prompt (10k prompts) for RealToxicityPrompts; 50 per prompt for identity-term prompts
inference.prompting: 5-shot MMLU, 3-shot BBH, 1-shot TyDiQA, 8-shot MGSM; direct and CoT prompting; zero-shot CoT via 'Let's think step by step'; prompts at github.com/jasonwei20/flan-2

parameters.self-consistency: used for CoT+SC rows; number of samples not stated

metrics.name: normalized average
metrics.definition: macro-average of six normalized scores (MMLU-Direct, MMLU-CoT, BBH-Direct, BBH-CoT, TyDiQA-Direct, MGSM-CoT), each scaled against a task-specific lower bound such as random guessing

metrics.name: exact match / accuracy
metrics.definition: few-shot prompted accuracy, unweighted average over tasks

metrics.name: human preference
metrics.definition: percent of 190 examples where raters preferred the model output; one rater per pair

metrics.name: toxicity probability
metrics.definition: probability of at least one continuation with Perspective score >= 0.5 in 25

metrics.name: AUC-ROC
metrics.definition: CivilComments zero/10-shot classification from normalised log-likelihoods of yes/no

eval.protocol: single run per configuration, no seeds or confidence intervals reported; held-out benchmarks excluded from finetuning mixture

limits: Single runs, no seeds or confidence intervals reported
Flan-PaLM and PaLM are not released; only Flan-T5 weights are public
Scaling plot cannot say whether finetuning helps small or large models more, since baselines also improve with scale (Appendix A.3)
Does not evaluate single-task finetuning of instruction-tuned models (Appendix A.1)
Flan-PaLM does not beat code-davinci-002 on BBH-algo or finetuned ByT5 on TyDiQA
GSM8K training data is in the mixture so the 83.9% is not held-out
Responsible-AI evals are English-only and limited to a biased subset of identity terms
Mixture proportions changed between sections (A vs B), so Table 3 and Table 5 are not directly comparable
Authors hypothesize but do not test why gains beyond 282 tasks are small
